source_used: Tech Policy Press, The Irish Times, Euronews (Reuters video not readable)
key_facts: International AI Summit held 14 Oct 2026 in Dublin, organised by Ireland's government as part of its EU Council presidency
Government launched a "Dublin Declaration" for trusted, safe and sovereign AI across Europe
Protesters outside and critics inside said independent and critical voices were lacking; a union representative was added to the agenda after lawmakers pressed
Microsoft president Brad Smith said there are more safety rules for ovens and cartons of milk than for AI
OpenAI chief financial officer Sarah Friar said firms should sell solutions rather than fear
EU executive vice-president Henna Virkkunen said the AI Office has started enforcing the rules
quote_evidence: “Selling fear is not a good way to come to the world. We have to sell solutions and solutions that feel transparent, open and honest,” Friar said.
In a speech at the event, Microsoft president Brad Smith called for stricter safety rules for AI, saying there were more safety rules for ovens and cartons of milk than there were for AI.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows the split between industry optimism and calls for firmer safety rules at Europe's main AI gathering.
notes: Reuters item is a video; could not read. Entry built by the desk from three outlets.
title: AI safety fault lines at the AI summit in Dublin
